summary: The prepared_gaia project is the most architecturally complete of the three versions, using the SPADE framework with genuine async agent behaviours, XMPP-style message passing, and a persistent SQLite database. However, it contains two critical security vulnerabilities — eval() is called on untrusted network message bodies in data_handler.py (lines 47 and 80) and services.py (line 38), and agent passwords are hardcoded as plain strings. Several key requirements are missing or broken: no alternative route mechanism exists, the matching logic between requests and available materials is incomplete, and multiple message targets reference non-existent agents. These critical issues require the system to be classified as failing.

findings.description: eval() is called directly on incoming network message bodies in three places. Any agent (or attacker who can send an XMPP message) can inject arbitrary Python code that executes with the full privileges of the receiving agent process.
findings.evidence: data_handler.py line 47: 'request_dict = eval(msg.body)'. data_handler.py line 80: 'match_dict = eval(msg.body)'. services.py line 38: 'special_notification_dict = eval(msg.body)'.

findings.description: All agent JIDs and passwords are hardcoded as plaintext in run_system.py. Any developer with access to the source code can authenticate as any agent in the system.
findings.evidence: run_system.py lines 51–57: PersonInNeedAgent('person_in_need@localhost', 'password123'), HelperAgent('helper@localhost', 'password123'), etc. — same password for all seven agents.

findings.description: TruckDriverAgent sends location updates to 'route_optimizer@localhost' (truck_driver.py line 42), but no RoutePlannerAgent or any other agent listens at that address. Location messages are sent to a non-existent recipient and silently discarded.
findings.evidence: truck_driver.py line 42: 'to="route_optimizer@localhost"'. No agent in run_system.py or the agents/ directory is initialised with the JID 'route_optimizer@localhost'.

findings.description: DataHandlerAgent.ProduceAvailableMaterialsBehaviour sends AvailableMaterials to 'matcher@localhost' (data_handler.py line 124), but no agent with that JID exists in the system. The materials never reach a matching component.
findings.evidence: data_handler.py line 124: 'to="matcher@localhost"'. run_system.py lines 51–57: no agent is assigned the JID 'matcher@localhost'.

findings.description: HelperAgent.ProduceRequestBehaviour sends AvailableMaterials to 'data_handler@localhost' (helper.py line 44), but DataHandlerAgent has no behaviour that listens for the subject 'AvailableMaterials'. These messages are silently ignored.
findings.evidence: helper.py line 44: 'to="data_handler@localhost"', subject='AvailableMaterials'. data_handler.py: only AwaitRequestBehaviour (subject='Request') and AwaitMatchInformationBehaviour (subject='MatchInformation') are registered — no handler for 'AvailableMaterials'.

findings.description: No mechanism for alternative route planning or route updates on accidents exists. There is no agent behaviour, data type, or message path that handles road blockages or computes alternative routes. Requirements 'Wyznaczanie alternatywnych tras przejazdu' and 'Aktualizacja obecnej trasy w razie wypadków losowych' are entirely absent.
findings.evidence: Entire agents/ directory reviewed: no method or behaviour related to blockage reporting, alternative routes, or route recalculation. Route is produced once in RoutePlannerAgent.ProduceRouteBehaviour and never updated.

findings.description: Resource matching logic is not implemented. DataHandlerAgent stores requests and available materials independently, but no agent reads both collections and produces a MatchInformation. The matching step — core to requirement 'Dopasowywanie dostępnych zasobów do potrzeb' — is missing.
findings.evidence: data_handler.py: AwaitMatchInformationBehaviour stores matches it receives but never creates them. No agent holds both requests and materials and compares them. project_structure.md line 13 references 'protocols.py' but that file does not exist in the codebase.

findings.description: project_structure.md references a core/protocols.py file that defines protocol definitions, but the file does not exist in the implementation. The README also claims GAIA methodology with defined protocols, which are unimplemented.
findings.evidence: project_structure.md line 13: '- protocols.py - Protocol definitions'. Glob of core/ directory finds only database.py, message_types.py, and __init__.py.

findings.description: RoutePlannerAgent.AwaitMatchInformationBehaviour receives match information but does nothing with it — the handler body contains only a comment and a pass-equivalent. Routes are generated independently of any actual match, making route assignment to deliveries non-functional.
findings.evidence: route_planner.py lines 33–38: 'if msg: self.agent.logger.info(...) # In a real system, this would process the match and generate route'.

findings.description: run_system.py bypasses the SPADE agent lifecycle entirely. Agents are instantiated but never started (agent.start() is not called). The simulation manually performs database operations and constructs message objects without using any agent behaviours, rendering the multi-agent architecture decorative.
findings.evidence: run_system.py lines 51–57: agents instantiated. Lines 63–143: simulation proceeds by calling db.add_request(), db.add_match(), etc. directly — no agent.start() or message passing.

findings.description: PersonInNeedAgent.SubscribeTruckDriverLocationBehaviour and SubscribeNotificationBehaviour create Template objects with subject/sender filters but do not call await self.receive(timeout=...), meaning behaviours will block indefinitely if no message arrives.
findings.evidence: person_in_need.py lines 55–73: 'msg = await self.receive(template)' with no timeout parameter.

findings.description: The database layer (database.py) uses parameterised SQL queries throughout, correctly protecting against SQL injection.
findings.evidence: database.py lines 51–62: 'await db.execute("INSERT OR REPLACE INTO requests ... VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)", (request.id, ...))'.

findings.description: The system uses SPADE's async CyclicBehaviour with asyncio.sleep for agent pacing, demonstrating correct non-blocking async design within individual agent behaviours.
findings.evidence: person_in_need.py line 53: 'await asyncio.sleep(10)'. helper.py line 50: 'await asyncio.sleep(15)'. notifier.py line 64: 'await asyncio.sleep(30)'.

findings.description: A structured set of domain message types (Request, AvailableMaterials, MatchInformation, Route, OptimizedRoute, Notification, SpecialNotification, TruckDriverLocation) is well-defined using Python dataclasses, covering all key system entities.
findings.evidence: core/message_types.py: eight dataclasses with typed fields and sensible defaults.

missing_requirements: Wyznaczanie alternatywnych tras przejazdu w razie wypadków losowych — no alternative route agent behaviour, data type, or message path exists anywhere in the codebase
Aktualizacja obecnej trasy w razie wypadków losowych — no route update mechanism on accidents; RoutePlannerAgent only produces a single static route
Zgłaszanie informacji o nieprzejezdnych drogach — no road blockage reporting mechanism; no agent role or behaviour for this function
Dopasowywanie dostępnych zasobów do potrzeb — matching logic between requests and available materials is absent; no agent produces MatchInformation
logical_inconsistencies: TruckDriverAgent sends to 'route_optimizer@localhost' but no such agent exists — location updates are silently lost
DataHandlerAgent sends AvailableMaterials to 'matcher@localhost' but no agent has that JID — materials produced by DataHandlerAgent never reach any matching component
HelperAgent sends AvailableMaterials to DataHandlerAgent but DataHandlerAgent has no behaviour registered to receive subject='AvailableMaterials'
project_structure.md references core/protocols.py which does not exist — the GAIA protocol layer is entirely absent from the implementation
run_system.py instantiates SPADE agents but never calls agent.start(), so all agent behaviours (CyclicBehaviour, etc.) never execute during the simulation
implementation_risks: CRITICAL: eval(msg.body) on XMPP messages allows any network participant to execute arbitrary Python code in the agent process
CRITICAL: all agents share the same hardcoded password 'password123', enabling credential stuffing and impersonation across the entire agent network

Silent message loss at three communication paths ('route_optimizer@localhost', 'matcher@localhost', AvailableMaterials to DataHandlerAgent) means the system appears to run while key workflows never complete
Blocking receive() calls without timeouts in PersonInNeedAgent can permanently stall agent behaviour loops if expected messages never arrive
